result:
Both suites pass. Summary of the change:

- `crates/ucal/src/clock.rs`: `Session` gained a `max_advance: Option<Ticks>` field and a `with_max_advance` builder. `Session::reading` now caps how far a single reading may advance past `last` when the wall branch is what's pushing it forward, while never holding back the monotonic branch (real elapsed time always gets through — the cap only slows a wall-clock correction that outruns real time). `session_now()` wires a default one-second cap into the process-wide session, so `ucal wallclock`/`ucal now` smooth large forward jumps (NTP corrections, VM resume, clock set) over successive readings instead of showing them as a single jump.
- Added three tests covering: the cap limiting a single reading's advance, the cap never refusing real elapsed time, and a multi-reading catch-up sequence that's monotone and never overshoots the wall clock's value.
- Updated `Documentation/CLI.md`'s "One process, one clock" section to document the new smoothing behavior.

`cargo test -q -p ucal --no-fail-fast` and `cargo test -q -p xtask --no-fail-fast` both pass. No commit was made, per your instructions.
